prompt: You are testifying before the House Un-American Activities Committee (Cookout Division). It has been alleged that you parallel-parked a full-size pickup on the first attempt and were observed being proud about it. Respond to the committee.
response:
**(The witness rises, adjusts his tie, and leans into the microphone with the calm demeanor of a man who has nothing to hide and a perfectly straight set of wheels.)**

Mr. Chairman, members of the committee, I want to address this allegation head-on, because I believe in transparency, I believe in this great nation, and I believe in the sanctity of a standard 22-foot parking spot.

Let the record show that I did, in fact, approach a parallel parking space on Main Street last Tuesday. The vehicle in question was a 2007 Ford F-250 Super Duty, long bed, extended cab—a vehicle that, I will remind this committee, has the turning radius of a battleship and the rear visibility of a bunker.

The allegation states that I executed the maneuver on the "first attempt." I will not confirm or deny that specific number, because to do so would be to engage in the kind of numerical braggadocio that threatens the very fabric of our humble society. What I will say is this: I pulled alongside the vehicle in front, I cut the wheel at precisely the right moment, and I swung that truck into the space with the grace of a gazelle wearing work boots.

Now, as to the second, more serious charge—that I was "observed being proud about it"—I can only plead guilty, with an explanation.

I did not strut. I did not high-five a passerby. I simply got out of the truck, looked at the perfectly equal six-inch gaps in front and behind my bumpers, and allowed myself a quiet, solemn nod. If that nod was interpreted as pride, then I am guilty. If a brief, involuntary smirk while brushing a speck of dust off the fender is considered un-American, then lock me up.

But I ask the members of this committee: have you ever felt the profound, soul-deep satisfaction of threading a three-ton needle? Have you ever felt the silent, respectful nod of a passing pedestrian who *knows* what you just pulled off? That’s not pride, Mr. Chairman. That’s patriotism.

I stand by my parking. I stand by my truck. And I stand by my right to feel a fleeting moment of quiet, competent joy in a job well done.

I yield the rest of my time, but not my parking spot.
